title: Peritumoral ultrasound features improve prediction of breast-cancer nodal metastasis
summary: DenseNet-121 neural networks and random-forest radiomics models were evaluated on ultrasound images from 479 women with pathology-confirmed breast cancer. Including tissue around the tumor improved axillary-node metastasis prediction: the combined-region image-only CNN had a reported test AUC of 0.912, compared with 0.748 for the tumor-only CNN. The combined CNN also reached AUC 0.95 in an additional 16-patient cohort described as prospective, but this single-center paper reports inconsistent training/test counts and does not establish clinical benefit or the biological basis of the imaging association.
ai_technology: DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network; random-forest radiomics with Boruta feature selection
organization: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Peking University Shenzhen Hospital; Ultimage Lab; Peng Cheng Laboratory

evidence.tested: A single-center study used 2,395 images from 479 patients and histopathologic nodal labels. The combined image-only CNN reported test AUC 0.912 versus 0.748 for tumor-only images; differences from corresponding radiomics models were not statistically significant. A further 16-patient cohort reported combined-CNN AUC 0.95.
evidence.unknown: The abstract/image-acquisition description gives training/test counts 343/136, whereas the population description/table gives 359/120. Locked-model timing before new outcomes in the additional cohort is not established by the reviewed Methods. The authors call for larger multicenter/different-machine studies and biological investigation; clinical benefit was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: DenseNet-121 learns image features to classify pathology-confirmed nodal metastasis; Boruta-selected radiomic features feed random forests. Comparing input regions identifies the study-specific predictive information gained from peritumoral tissue.

source_review.scope: Original full-text source: abstract, publication metadata, relevant model/feature selection and validation Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary files not assessed.
